candidates.description: Participation in an international consulting project improves self-reported entrepreneurial competencies
candidates.citation_sentence: In 2013, Michael Morris and his colleagues reported in the Journal of Small Business Management that 40 students reported a significant increase in 9 of 13 entrepreneurial competencies following a six-week international consulting project with disadvantaged entrepreneurs in South Africa (Morris et al., 2013b).
candidates.notes: In-study replication cohort (Fall 2017); the desired interaction effect was present for only one competency (not one of the original three), and the repeated measures model found no class-by-time interaction. The authors explicitly frame this as a failure to replicate the original findings. The second cohort (Fall 2017) is an in-study replication of the first cohort and is excluded as a within-paper replication per codebook rules. The first cohort's result is inconclusive: some competencies showed significant increases but the main interaction effect was present in only 3 of 13 competencies, and authors describe results as 'very limited support' and 'unable to reliably increase any of the 13 competencies.' The replication_type is coded as conceptual because the authors explicitly call it a 'systematic/conceptual replication' and the manipulation differs fundamentally (classroom curriculum vs. international consulting project).
